mike: Heads-up — need a short sync on tenant isolation + egress guarantees for hosted/dedicated/private. Found some edge cases when customers require on-prem sidecars and strict egress allowlists.

julia: ok, can you sketch the main concerns?

mike: main ones:
- network egress control per-tenant
- control-plane vs data-plane telemetry separation
- KMS/HSM key access model
- SLA & routing when private can't reach hosted fallback

sam: quick +1. Are we still assuming private has full routing to control plane? some customers want offline attestable control plane.

mike: no, that's the problem. private can be either 'connected' or 'airgapped'. For connected we can use normal control-plane APIs; for airgapped we need a different handshake and local telemetry sink.

julia: propose we add explicit 'connectivity_mode' on the manifest: connected | sync-proxy | airgapped. That way adapters know what features to expose.

sam: example manifest piece? 

mike: sure:
```
connectivity_mode: "sync-proxy" # forwards control-plane ops over a lightweight relay
egress_policy:
  allowlists:
    - 10.0.0.0/8
    - api.redwood.example.com:443
kms_mode: "local-hsm"
```

rachael: instrumentation: we need to avoid sending per-tenant PII to hosted telemetry when private is in airgapped mode. Suggest a telemetry-privacy flag and hashed identifiers.

julia: agree. also we must document which APIs require direct control-plane reachability vs async file transfer (e.g., model bundles, logs).

mike: tradeoffs:
- More config complexity for customers
- Simpler control plane logic if we treat private as separate product
- But operational overhead for dual code paths

sam: question on SLA: if private falls back to hosted due to capacity, is that allowed by default? i think customers will want an explicit opt-in.

rachael: yes opt-in only. Need UI + policy for can-fallback.

julia: next steps: write RFC with manifest additions + protocol for sync-proxy + telemetry redaction rules. @mike can you draft? target EOW.

mike: will do. pinging @ops-bot to create a tracking ticket.

ops-bot: created ticket INF-1248: 'private-deploy: connectivity modes & egress policy RFC' — https://go/repo/INF-1248 :spiral_notepad:

mike: thanks. if anyone has strong objections to connectivity_mode enum or naming speak now. otherwise i'll start the RFC draft.

sam: no objections from me. +1 to sync-proxy term.

rachael: +1

julia: +1 :rocket:
